headline: Energy Leads a Cautious Friday as Geopolitical Tension Keeps Risk Appetite in Check
body_html:
Equity markets are drifting in mixed territory at midday Friday, with declining issues outpacing advancers 312-to-231 across our 549-name universe. The dominant theme is unmistakable: elevated crude prices, fuelled by U.S. threats of an indefinite blockade of Iran and fresh attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, are funnelling money into the Energy sector — the session's clear leader with a gain of roughly 45 basis points — while simultaneously capping broader risk appetite and weighing on growth-sensitive names.

Sector leadership is thin but coherent. Materials are modestly higher, lifted in part by metallurgical coal producer Alpha Metallurgical Resources, up 3.4%. Technology and healthcare are the session's soft spots, with Software and Healthcare each off roughly 40-plus basis points. Semiconductors are also under pressure, sliding about 23 basis points, as Applied Materials sheds 3.5% and connectivity chipmaker Credo Technology drops nearly 4%. Optical-networking names Ciena and Coherent are both lower by roughly 3% apiece.

The standout mover of the day is intellectual-property licensor Adeia, surging 5.5% with no obvious headline catalyst — the kind of idiosyncratic pop worth watching into the close. Copart is also quietly strong, up 4%. Into the final hours, traders should monitor Hormuz shipping headlines and Treasury-yield direction for any late-session shift in tone.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Flashpoint Drives Oil Toward Weekly Gain
briefs.body: Crude is on track for a positive week after the United States threatened to indefinitely blockade Iran and reports emerged of two additional vessel attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. The standoff has capped shipping traffic through the strategically vital waterway, keeping a floor under oil prices and lifting Energy equities at the expense of broader market sentiment.

briefs.headline: Treasury Yields Climb as Washington Turns Up Sanctions Pressure on Tehran
briefs.body: U.S. government bond yields are rising Friday as Washington signals a further tightening of economic sanctions against Iran. Higher yields are adding a secondary headwind for rate-sensitive growth stocks, contributing to the softness visible across the Software and Healthcare sectors at midday.

briefs.headline: Gold Eases From Two-Month Peak as Inflation Momentum Fades
briefs.body: Bullion is pausing near recent highs after an inflation-driven rally showed signs of losing steam. The pullback suggests some tactical profit-taking among safe-haven buyers, even as geopolitical risk from the Middle East and competing U.S.-Iran narratives remain squarely in the background.

briefs.headline: Optical-Networking Names Take a Midday Beating
briefs.body: Ciena and Coherent are each lower by roughly 3% in Friday trading, dragging the Networking-Optical pocket into the red. The declines come without a single company-specific catalyst, pointing instead to sector-wide rotation away from hardware names tied to data-infrastructure spending as sentiment softens.

briefs.headline: China Flags Taiwan Drills as Political Theater, Adding to Regional Uncertainty
briefs.body: Beijing dismissed Taiwan's annual military exercises as a wasteful display rather than a genuine security measure, ratcheting up rhetorical pressure ahead of what is typically a sensitive period in cross-strait relations. The comment adds another layer of geopolitical noise for investors tracking Asia-Pacific risk alongside the Middle East situation.

briefs.headline: Air India Safety Review Widens After Flight-Control Scare Documented by Airbus
briefs.body: An Airbus analysis confirmed that an Air India A320 temporarily lost critical flight controls during a recent operation, broadening scrutiny of maintenance and operational practices at the carrier. The findings are likely to intensify regulatory oversight of the airline and could affect near-term sentiment around global aviation supply chains.
